titulo: Does oil in the pasta water stop sticking?
receta: mito + regla para guardar (qué sí evita que se pegue)
destinatario: Se lo manda alguien que cocina pasta a su papá o mamá que siempre le echa un chorro de aceite al agua.

interaccion.guardar: Pasta not sticking: no oil. Hard boil + stir, especially at the start (America's Test Kitchen).
interaccion.comentar: Do you put oil in your pasta water? Yes or no?

fuentes: America's Test Kitchen: Making Your Pasta Water Work for You

frases.texto: You pour oil in your pasta water so the noodles don't stick.

frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: America's Test Kitchen says oil in the cooking water does not help the pasta from sticking to itself.
So what does? A hard boil, and stirring.
Especially at the start of cooking, when the noodles are fresh in the pot and want to clump together.
Heads up: this is about sticking. Oil is still fine in a sauce or a skillet, it just isn't doing anything in the pot.
Save this for your next pasta night: no oil. Hard boil. Stir at the start.
Do you put oil in your pasta water? Yes or no?
Send this to the person who has poured oil in the pot for years.
